response.query: What gold-standard measurement SOPs and target inter-annotator agreement thresholds (IoU, ICC) should we adopt for crack width/depth and spalled volume, and how will conflicts be adjudicated?
response.answer: Use ICC for crack width/depth and IoU for spalled volume; aim for ICC > 0.8 and IoU > 0.75; conflicts adjudicated by senior annotator.

results.title: Inter-Annotator Agreement: a key metric in Labeling
results.content: An Inter-Annotator Agreement (IAA) is a measure of the agreement or consistency between each annotation produced by different annotators working on the same task or data set, as part of the preparation of a training dataset for AI. In the field of Artificial Intelligence (AI), the Inter-Annotator Agreement plays a leading role in ensuring the quality and reliability of annotated data sets, used to train and evaluate AI models. The Inter Annotator Agreement can be used to assess the quality of annotations in annotated data sets and identify areas where models produce incorrect results. By proactively using the Inter-Annotator Agreement, AI specialists or Data Scientists can ensure the quality and consistency of evaluations in various fields, which reinforces the validity of the analyses and, potentially, the performance of the models. By measuring the consistency between annotators, the IAA ensures that data sets are reliable and free of bias, thus contributing to the effectiveness of the AI models developed.

IAA is a statistical measure that quantifies the level of agreement among annotators. IAA metrics should be used to evaluate annotator consistency and identify areas for improvement. By understanding the factors that influence IAA, employing strategies to improve IAA, and following best practices, annotators and researchers can achieve high consistency and accuracy in linguistic annotation. Inter-Annotator Agreement (IAA) is a statistical measure that quantifies the level of agreement among annotators when labeling or annotating data. IAA can be improved by developing clear and concise annotation guidelines, providing annotator training and feedback, using multiple annotators, and adjudicating disagreements. Best practices for achieving high IAA include pilot testing and refining annotation guidelines, monitoring annotator performance, and using IAA metrics to evaluate annotator consistency.

results.title: Inter-Annotator Agreement (IAA) | UBIAI LLM Fine-tuning
results.content: # Inter-Annotator Agreement (IAA). Ensuring consistency and identifying conflicts between annotators is crucial for the success of any annotation project. UBIAI’s Inter-Annotator Agreement (IAA) feature allows you to evaluate team performance by distributing the same documents to multiple annotators. >   + Documents to be distributed for annotation. > * **Finalize and Distribute**: Save the IAA task, and documents will be assigned to the chosen annotators for evaluation. > * **Annotator Management**: Add or remove annotators from an ongoing IAA task by clicking the "Add Member to IAA Task" button. > * **Document-Level Scores**: Click on individual IAA scores to see detailed results for each document, offering granular insights into annotator performance. **Open the Conflict Report**: Select a document from the list of annotated files. UBIAI’s Union Merge feature allows you to merge annotations from multiple annotators into the master project. > * **Resolve Conflicts**: After clicking the **Merge Documents** button, a new window will display any annotation conflicts.
